input: Set up a weekly pantry audit to reduce waste

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the audit covers only dry goods, or also fridge, freezer, and spices changes the checklist complexity and time required.
Whether this is for one person, a couple, or a family affects how items are tracked, who is responsible, and how much volume is involved.
The best day and time to run the audit depends on when the user shops, so the audit can directly inform the shopping list.
How much time the user can dedicate each week determines how thorough the audit process can realistically be.
Whether the user prefers a physical checklist, spreadsheet, or an app changes what system gets built and how likely they are to stick with it.
Understanding the biggest waste driver (forgetting items exist, ignoring expiry dates, over-buying) focuses the audit on what will actually reduce waste.
Knowing whether they want a ready-to-use template or a step-by-step setup guide determines the immediate first deliverable.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a weekly pantry audit to reduce waste
gold.taskDescription: Build a repeatable weekly routine for checking pantry contents, tracking expiry dates, and acting on findings to minimise food waste at home.

questions.title: Which storage areas should the audit cover?
questions.description: Should the audit include only the dry-goods pantry, or also the fridge, freezer, and spice collection?

questions.title: How many people does this household feed?
questions.description: Is this for one person living alone, a couple, or a larger family — and will others participate in running the audit?

questions.title: Which day do you usually do your grocery shopping?
questions.description: Knowing the regular shopping day helps schedule the audit immediately before it, so findings directly shape the shopping list.

questions.title: How many minutes can you spend on this each week?
questions.description: A realistic time budget — 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes — determines how detailed the audit process can be.

questions.title: Do you prefer paper, a spreadsheet, or an app?
questions.description: The preferred tracking format determines what kind of system or template gets built and how it fits into existing habits.

questions.title: What is your main source of food waste right now?
questions.description: Is waste mostly caused by forgetting items exist, missing expiry dates, or consistently over-buying certain categories?

questions.title: Do you want a ready template or a full setup guide?
questions.description: Should the output be a filled-in, ready-to-use audit checklist, or a step-by-step guide for building the system from scratch?
